hook: You may need fewer fans than you think

insight.title: 1,000 True Fans
paras: Kevin Kelly’s 1,000 True Fans is a creator-economics heuristic: a sustainable business may need a smaller group of committed direct supporters, not a gigantic passive audience. The useful part is not the number 1,000; it is the unit-economics calculation.

Use required supporters = target annual income ÷ annual gross profit per supporter. A $100,000 target at $100 gross profit each suggests 1,000 supporters. At only $20 each, it becomes 5,000. This is a planning model, not a viral guarantee; price, margin, retention, direct reach, and operating costs all change the answer.

insight.visualCaption: The audience target changes when value per supporter changes.
after: For Daily Insight, stop treating raw reach as the primary score. Track returning learners, completed lessons, saves, direct replies, and referrals—the behaviors that reveal a committed learning audience.

For StoryOS or your consulting practice, choose an income target and estimate the annual gross profit from one genuinely engaged customer. Divide the first by the second. Then ask: are you building more reach, or increasing the value and retention of the people already leaning in?

lab.title: Calculate Your Real Audience
paras: A concrete denominator turns a fuzzy audience ambition into a business-model question.
lab.exercise: Pick one project and write three numbers: target annual income, annual gross profit per committed supporter, and the division result. Then test the result at half and double the profit per supporter. Say: “My audience target is not a follower count; it is this value-and-retention equation.”

storyVideoPlan.style: Warm editorial storybook animation with hand-painted gouache and risograph texture, bold cobalt, amber, coral and teal shapes, one recurring adult protagonist named Maya, no photorealism, no logos, no spoken characters
storyVideoPlan.narration: Maya has fifty thousand followers, yet her studio still struggles to pay its bills. The audience number is misleading. A smaller circle returns, buys her workshops, and brings friends. Those repeat supporters carry the business. Kevin Kelly’s One Thousand True Fans is a useful heuristic, not magic or a promise of virality. The calculation is simple: divide target annual income by annual gross profit per supporter. One hundred thousand divided by one hundred equals one thousand. At twenty dollars profit, it takes five thousand. Price, margin, retention, and direct reach change the answer. For Daily Insight, track returning learners, completed lessons, saves, replies, and referrals. Build for depth before chasing reach.

blocks.narration: Maya has fifty thousand followers, yet her warm studio still struggles to pay its bills. The giant audience number is misleading.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 warm editorial storybook animation matching the supplied Maya reference exactly: adult woman with short dark curly bob, teal sweater, ochre trousers, cobalt-amber-coral-teal gouache and risograph texture. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, with motion from frame one. Shot 1 WIDE: Maya works at a warm creative studio desk while a huge cloud of tiny follower dots swirls above her phone. Shot 2 HIGH ANGLE: unpaid bills slide across the desk as the follower cloud keeps growing. Shot 3 CLOSE-UP: the phone counter races upward while Maya's worried eyes reflect it. Shot 4 LOW ANGLE: the enormous counter shadow overwhelms the small studio. Shot 5 MEDIUM: Maya lowers the phone and looks toward a small glowing circle offscreen. Characters emote and gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

blocks.narration: A much smaller circle returns each month, buys her workshops, and brings friends. Those repeat supporters carry more weight than casual scrollers.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm gouache-risograph editorial storybook world and identical Maya character. Shot 2 CLOSE-UP: hands exchange workshop tickets and handmade prints. Shot 3 OVERHEAD: the same supporters return around a round table month after month as calendar pages flip. Shot 4 SIDE ANGLE: one supporter enthusiastically brings a friend into the circle. Shot 5 WIDE: the small circle glows brightly while the distant follower cloud fades. blocks.narration: Kevin Kelly’s One Thousand True Fans is a useful heuristic, not magic, a fixed threshold, or any promise of virality.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm gouache-risograph editorial storybook style. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, immediate motion. Shot 1 MACRO: one glowing supporter token pulses in Maya's hand. Shot 2 TOP-DOWN: many warm tokens ripple outward into an organized ring. Shot 3 WIDE: the ring resolves into a symbolic crowd of one thousand lights around Maya's studio. Shot 4 HIGH ANGLE: a glittering magic-wand shortcut appears, cracks, and dissolves to show this is not magic. Shot 5 MEDIUM: Maya calmly weighs the glowing supporter ring against a faded viral rocket symbol. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

blocks.narration: Divide target annual income by annual gross profit per supporter. One hundred thousand divided by one hundred equals one thousand committed supporters.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm editorial storybook animation. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, motion from frame one. Shot 1 OVERHEAD: Maya places a large gold income token above a hand-drawn division line. Shot 2 MACRO: a coral supporter-value token slides beneath the line. Shot 3 SIDE ANGLE: the tokens click into a simple mechanical calculator. Shot 4 CLOSE-UP: the machine releases ten neat bundles of one hundred glowing supporter lights. Shot 5 WIDE: one thousand lights form a stable warm bridge supporting Maya's studio. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text or numerals, no logos.

blocks.narration: At only twenty dollars profit each, that same goal needs five thousand supporters. Price, margin, retention, and direct reach change everything.

Shot 1 CLOSE-UP: the coral value token visibly shrinks in Maya's palm. Shot 2 LOW ANGLE: the calculator gears spin much faster. Shot 3 WIDE: the supporter-light bridge stretches five times farther across the studio. Shot 4 TOP-DOWN: four tactile levers for value, margin, return visits, and direct connection slide to different positions. Shot 5 MEDIUM: Maya adjusts one lever and watches the required crowd expand and contract. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

steal.line: Build for depth before you buy reach.
paras: Use this whenever a growth discussion jumps straight to follower counts. It redirects the conversation toward value per person and the behaviors that reveal durable demand.
example: In a Daily Insight review: “Before we chase more reach, which signal proves the people already here are returning, finishing, saving, replying, or referring?”
